edges.notes: Fedora ships Linux kernel packages for supported architectures as part of the distribution.
Fedora on standard ports uses glibc as the C library alongside the dynamic linker.
systemd is the default init and service manager on Fedora editions per Fedora documentation themes.
Fedora services are expressed as systemd unit files and drop-ins on default systemd installs.
Fedora userland binaries and shared libraries are ELF on typical Linux targets.
GCC toolchain packages are central to Fedora development and package build flows.
GNU binutils participate in standard Fedora RPM build and link flows.
g++-built packages link GNU libstdc++ above glibc on typical Fedora GNU/Linux flows.
Clang/LLVM packages are available from Fedora repositories for alternative compiler stacks.
Official fedora OCI images are common glibc-based bases; Docker pulls and runs them like other Linux images.
CRI/containerd nodes run Fedora-based workload images pulled as OCI artifacts.
Kubernetes nodes and pods frequently use Fedora-class or RHEL-family images on Linux; not exclusive.
Fedora bases are packaged as OCI image rootfs layers conforming to OCI image layout conventions.
Substitutable Linux distribution defaults for containers and servers (glibc/systemd vs musl/OpenRC field patterns).
Fedora Project innovation and ecosystem practices feed CentOS Stream as the public upstream development branch adjacent to RHEL minor streams.
Fedora Project innovation feeds Red Hat Enterprise Linux packaging and technology streams with distinct enterprise cadence and support policy.
